subject: AWS Marketplace listing: buyer-path friction & field enablement
messages:
From: Michael Chan <michael.chan@acme-corp.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask: AWS listing copy and buyer path questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the intro to Redwood last week — Acme’s infra team liked the demo.
We’re drafting the internal procurement packet and I want to make sure the public AWS product page won't create extra friction for our legal/buyers.

Two quick things:
- If we list a "Buy" CTA (standard purchase), will it show price tiers or require contacting sales for enterprise pricing? We want a clear trial->purchase path.
- For Private Offers: does Redwood need to opt-in on the listing or is that managed via the Seller Console? Will Private Offers be visible to field sellers for co-sell?

Attached is a short checklist of items procurement is asking for (no PII): budget expectations, SLA language, and data residency callouts.

Can you point me to the right copy variant and timeline? We're aiming to have procurement sign-off by 5/21.

Thanks,
Michael
Acme Corp — Senior Cloud Architect

Attachment: acme_procurement_checklist.csv (csv)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask: AWS listing copy and buyer path questions

Hi Michael —

Thanks for flagging these. Quick answers up-front, followed by next steps and a copy attachment.

- Buy CTA vs Private Offer: The public "Buy" path shows the pricing tiers you publish on the AWS page. For enterprise deals where you need negotiated terms, we use Private Offers (created in Seller Console). Private Offers are not shown on the public page but the Seller Console and our sales ops can associate them with a listing so field sellers can view and promote them during outreach.

- Visibility to field sellers: Yes — with co-sell enabled and the appropriate entitlement metadata, field teams can see private offers and attach them to opportunities. We should include an explicit "Request private offer" flow in the page copy and in the co-sell playbook.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I'm attaching draft_listing_copy_v2.docx with a lean public page variant and a variant that surfaces a "Request private offer" CTA and sample SLA footnote.
2) Marissa, can you confirm the co-sell blurb for the product page and an example pricing callout? (see inline comments in the draft)
3) Aditya — please coordinate the assets we need to push to AWS Seller Central (SKUs, entitlement map, PKG manifest) and target 5/20 for submission so Acme procurement has time.

If that timeline works I can also provide a short field kit (one-pager + email template) to hand to Acme's buyer-facing teams.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Marketplace GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachment: draft_listing_copy_v2.docx (docx)

Nice, Kim — added a few tactical suggestions below (copied into the draft as comments).

High-level edits for listing copy:
- Lead with a one-line value prop that speaks to buyers: "Deploy reliable LLM inference with predictable latency and cost" (call out Dedicated & Private as options).
- Add a single line under pricing: "Usage-based pricing examples: 10k tokens/min = $X/day" — this helps procurement with rough cost modeling.
- Include a short bullet for compliance: "SOC 2 Type II; optional VPC/on‑prem install" (procurement asks this first).

Co-sell / field enablement:
- Add a "Request private offer" CTA that triggers a short form (email link or SFDC record) so sellers can initiate PO requests.
- We should include 2 quick one-pagers for sellers: (1) Procurement talking points, (2) Tech convo checklist (latency, isolation, data residency). I'll draft these tonight.

One small language nit: replace "Private control plane" with "Private control plane (VPC or on‑prem)" — clearer for buyers.

I'll inline the text edits in the doc and put a draft of the two one-pagers in GDrive.

—Marissa

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the context — we reviewed the attached draft. A few compliance/operational items to note before submission:

1) SKU and pricing format: Per marketplace rules, SKU must be alphanumeric, 8-12 chars. Usage-based SKUs need a clear metering dimension and samples of rate calculation.
2) Private Offers: You will create the private offer in Seller Central and then provide the Offer ID to your buyer. To make private offers discoverable to AWS field sellers, submit the co-sell opt-in checkbox during offer creation and attach the partner ID.
3) Required artifacts: We need (a) the published product page copy, (b) sample invoice, (c) SOC2 certificate or an attestation. If you prefer, upload these into the Partner Portal and then share the Drive link.
4) AMI/container guidance: see attached marketplace_ami_guidelines.pdf — keep the Image tag and sellerid fields consistent.

We recommend submitting by 2027-05-20 for listing to be live before end of month. If you want we can schedule a short 30-min checklist call next Tue to walk through the Seller Central steps.

Regards,
Nina Patel
AWS Marketplace Onboarding

Attachment: marketplace_ami_guidelines.pdf (pdf)
